page: Amazon Web Services m5n.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 64 vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at a base clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The instance is configured with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration instructions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES cryptography, and BMI2 bit manipulation. It does not bundle dedicated GPUs or local instance storage, requiring remote Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent disk operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong memory throughput alongside balanced multi-threaded compute capabilities. Potentially uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 213.54 GB/sec, while write operations achieve 93.42 GB/sec, placing memory transfer capabilities in the upper performance tier. In contrast, single-core execution metrics across Geekbench, stress-ng, and compression tests register lower relative to contemporary high-frequency architectures. Multi-core operations scale reliably, evidenced by 50.94 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and consistent middle-tier scores across PassMark CPU routines and static web serving tests.

The primary architectural distinction of this instance is its 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Resource allocation suits data-intensive, network-bound environments including intermediate caching tiers, distributed message brokers, ETL processing pipelines, and high-throughput application serving where remote network storage or intra-cluster communication demands substantial line-rate bandwidth.
description: Amazon Web Services m5n.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor. It is equipped with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores operating at 3.1 GHz, paired with 256 GB of DDR4 memory. The platform includes no local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on remote network storage. A standout hardware feature is its 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, supported by AVX-512 VNNI vector instruction sets. Benchmark evaluations indicate strong uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 213 GB/sec for reads and 93 GB/sec for writes, alongside mid-tier multi-threaded compute performance and Redis throughput exceeding 50 million operations per second. However, single-core benchmark metrics remain in lower quartiles. The instance is designed for network-heavy general-purpose enterprise tasks, cluster caching layers, distributed databases, and high-volume backend microservices.
